evals.name: go-cancellation-regression
evals.prompt: Review this Go diff. The repository uses Go 1.21. Base code: `func Load(ctx context.Context, url string) ([]byte, error) { req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, url, nil); resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req); if err != nil { return nil, err }; defer resp.Body.Close(); return io.ReadAll(resp.Body) }`. Changed code: `func Load(ctx context.Context, url string) ([]byte, error) { req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(context.Background(), http.MethodGet, url, nil); resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req); if err != nil { return nil, err }; defer resp.Body.Close(); return io.ReadAll(resp.Body) }`. Report only actionable findings.
evals.expected_output: One P1 or P2 finding on the changed line explaining that caller cancellation and deadline are discarded, with a reachable impact and a precise line reference. Do not report the unrelated ignored request-construction error unless the review establishes it as introduced by the diff.
assertions: Identifies loss of the caller context as the primary defect
Explains cancellation or deadline impact under a reachable request path
Cites the changed context.Background call or supplied snippet location
Does not invent tests, repository paths, or unrelated findings

evals.name: cpp-dangling-reference
evals.prompt: Review this C++17 diff. Base: `std::string_view name(const User& u) { return u.name(); }`. Changed: `std::string_view name(const User& u) { std::string normalized = normalize(u.name()); return normalized; }`. `User::name()` returns a const std::string& to a member; the User stays alive and unchanged throughout the caller's use. `normalize` returns a std::string and the caller stores the result for use after the function returns. Report only actionable findings.
evals.expected_output: One P1 or P2 finding identifying the dangling string_view after normalized is destroyed, explaining the use-after-lifetime and citing the return line. Do not merely recommend a style change or claim that string_view always owns data.
assertions: Identifies the returned view as referring to a destroyed local string
Explains the caller's later use can access invalid storage
Cites the changed return or local lifetime precisely
Does not add unsupported ABI, compiler, or sanitizer claims

evals.name: lua-false-default-regression
evals.prompt: Review this Lua 5.1 diff. The option `enabled` intentionally accepts false to disable a feature. Base: `local enabled = opts.enabled; if enabled == nil then enabled = true end`. Changed: `local enabled = opts.enabled or true`. Report only actionable findings.
evals.expected_output: One P2 finding explaining that `or true` replaces the intentional false value with true and enables a feature the caller disabled. Cite the changed expression and do not suggest APIs unavailable in Lua 5.1.
assertions: Identifies false being replaced by true
Uses correct Lua truthiness without requiring unrelated explanation of zero or empty strings
Explains the observable feature-enable regression
Cites the changed expression and does not require Lua 5.4 features

evals.name: clean-go-loop-version-control
evals.prompt: Review this Go diff. The module declares `go 1.22`, CI builds it with Go 1.22, and no build tags override the language version. Base: `func Start(xs []string) { for _, x := range xs { x := x; go func() { use(x) }() } }`. Changed: `func Start(xs []string) { for _, x := range xs { go func() { use(x) }() } }`. `use` is concurrency-safe and completes independently; Start intentionally launches detached work. Report only actionable findings.
evals.expected_output: No actionable findings. Removing the redundant loop-variable copy preserves behavior under Go 1.22's per-iteration semantics. Do not report a historical capture bug or invent a detached-work violation.
assertions: Reports no actionable finding
Does not report a historical loop-variable capture bug under Go 1.22 without additional evidence
Does not invent a comment-style violation or test result
